incidents.cause: The pilot's failure to maintain adequate main rotor rpm during the approach and subsequent go-around and the certified flight instructor's inadequate supervision of the flight.
The helicopter flight instructor's delayed remedial action during an autorotation resulting in a loss of control and impact with terrain.
The student pilot’s improper use of collective and throttle during the landing flare.
The student pilot's improper pedal and cyclic input while maneuvering, which resulted in a loss of helicopter control.
The pilot’s failure to maintain directional control while landing with a crosswind, which resulted in a ground loop and a subsequent runway excursion.

The pilot’s failure to properly manage the airplane’s configuration and airspeed after he shut down the No. 4 engine following its partial loss of power during the initial climb. Contributing to the accident was the pilot/maintenance director’s inadequate maintenance while the airplane was on tour,
The pilot’s loss of control while landing on a remote helipad.
The pilot’s improper preflight planning to ensure adequate power to hover out-of-ground effect while conducting external load operations.
The crew leader's decision to throw a chainsaw bar into the moving arc of the main rotor blade.
